title: Anticoagulant-associated bleeding: reversal
subject: haematology-oncology
summary: Classify the bleed; for major or critical-site bleeding stop the anticoagulant and reverse it: warfarin with vitamin K 5 to 10 mg IV plus 4-factor PCC dosed by INR, dabigatran with idarucizumab 5 g, factor Xa inhibitors with 4F-PCC (andexanet is largely unavailable), and heparins with protamine.

sections.title: Assess the bleed (ACC 2020)
items: Major bleed if any: haemodynamic instability (SBP below 90 mmHg, fall of more than 40 mmHg, MAP below 65 mmHg, or postural drop), bleeding at a critical site, Hb fall of 2 g/dL or more, or need for 2 or more red cell units.
Critical sites: intracranial, intraocular, spinal, airway, pericardial, thoracic, intra-abdominal, retroperitoneal, intra-articular, and intramuscular with compartment syndrome.
Record the anticoagulant, dose, time of last dose, creatinine clearance, and any antiplatelet, NSAID or interacting drug.
Non-major bleeding: local measures and supportive care; reversal agents are not indicated for DOACs. For warfarin, consider vitamin K 2 to 5 mg orally or IV.

sections.title: Immediate management of major bleeding
items: ABC, two large-bore cannulae, crossmatch, and activate the major haemorrhage protocol if needed.
Stop the anticoagulant and any antiplatelet agent. Arrange source control early: compression, endoscopy, interventional radiology or surgery.
Give the specific reversal agent without waiting for coagulation results when the history is clear, especially in intracranial haemorrhage.
Activated charcoal 50 g orally if a DOAC was taken within the last 2 to 4 hours and the airway is protected.

Send FBC, PT/INR, APTT, fibrinogen, renal function and group and screen. A normal PT or APTT does not exclude a clinically relevant DOAC effect (especially apixaban); use calibrated anti-Xa or dilute thrombin time if available.

sections.title: Warfarin and other vitamin K antagonists
items: Vitamin K 5 to 10 mg IV by slow infusion for every major bleed; always give it with PCC because the PCC effect wears off before warfarin does.
4-factor PCC dosed by INR: INR 2 to below 4: 25 units/kg (maximum 2500 units); INR 4 to 6: 35 units/kg (maximum 3500 units); INR above 6: 50 units/kg (maximum 5000 units).
Alternative fixed-dose PCC: 1000 units for non-intracranial major bleeding, 1500 units for intracranial haemorrhage.
Recheck INR after the infusion and give further PCC if reversal is inadequate.
If 4F-PCC is unavailable: FFP 10 to 15 mL/kg with vitamin K. It is slower (thawing, volume) and carries TACO and TRALI risk.
Acenocoumarol, widely used in India, is reversed the same way.

sections.title: Direct oral anticoagulants
items: Dabigatran: idarucizumab 5 g IV (two 2.5 g vials given no more than 15 minutes apart). Consider a second dose if bleeding persists with evidence of residual dabigatran.
Dabigatran without idarucizumab: PCC or activated PCC 50 units/kg (maximum 4000 units); haemodialysis removes dabigatran and may help when levels are high, particularly with renal impairment.
Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban: 4F-PCC 2000 units IV fixed dose (ACC 2020) or 50 units/kg (EHRA 2021), with a further 25 units/kg if bleeding continues.

Andexanet alfa was preferred by ACC 2020 but was withdrawn from the US market in December 2025 after excess thrombosis, and is not marketed in India. Where still available, use only for life-threatening bleeding on specialist advice.
Reversal is rarely needed if the last dose was long ago relative to renal function; half-life lengthens as creatinine clearance falls.

sections.title: Heparins
items: Unfractionated heparin: protamine 1 mg per 100 units of heparin given in the previous 2 to 3 hours (maximum 50 mg) by slow IV injection over 10 minutes. If APTT stays prolonged, give 0.5 mg per 100 units.
Enoxaparin given within 8 hours: protamine 1 mg per 1 mg enoxaparin (maximum 50 mg); given 8 to 12 hours ago: 0.5 mg per 1 mg. Reversal of LMWH is only partial.
Protamine can cause hypotension, bradycardia and anaphylaxis (risk higher with fish allergy or previous protamine-containing insulin); give slowly with monitoring.
Fondaparinux has no specific antidote: seek haematology advice.

sections.title: Restarting anticoagulation
items: Most patients with an ongoing indication (AF with stroke risk, mechanical valve, recent VTE) benefit from restarting once haemostasis is secure. Decide jointly with the patient and relevant specialists.
Delay restart if the bleed was at a critical site, rebleeding risk is high, an invasive procedure is planned, or the patient is nil by mouth.
Correct contributors before restarting: supratherapeutic INR, drug interactions, declining renal function, unnecessary antiplatelets or NSAIDs; consider switching agent if the bleed was drug-related.
Reassess the need for aspirin in stable coronary disease and for dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI or ACS.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: PCC for warfarin without vitamin K: the INR rebounds within hours.
Using FFP first line when PCC is available, or waiting for an INR before reversing in intracranial haemorrhage.
Giving reversal agents for minor DOAC-associated bleeding; supportive care and time usually suffice.
Forgetting that reversal exposes the patient to thrombosis: plan thromboprophylaxis and restart early when safe.

drugs.name: Vitamin K (phytomenadione)
drugs.dose: Major bleeding: 5 to 10 mg IV by slow infusion. Non-major bleeding: 2 to 5 mg orally or IV
drugs.notes: Always combine with PCC for major warfarin-associated bleeding.

drugs.name: 4-factor PCC (warfarin)
drugs.dose: INR 2 to below 4: 25 units/kg (max 2500); INR 4 to 6: 35 units/kg (max 3500); INR above 6: 50 units/kg (max 5000). Or fixed 1000 units (1500 units for ICH)

drugs.name: 4-factor PCC (factor Xa inhibitors)
drugs.dose: 2000 units IV fixed dose (ACC 2020), or 50 units/kg IV (EHRA 2021); further 25 units/kg if bleeding continues
drugs.notes: Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban when andexanet is unavailable.

drugs.name: Idarucizumab
drugs.dose: 5 g IV (2 x 2.5 g, no more than 15 minutes apart)
drugs.notes: Dabigatran only. Second dose may be reasonable if bleeding persists with residual drug effect.

drugs.name: Andexanet alfa
drugs.dose: Low dose: 400 mg IV bolus at 30 mg/min then 4 mg/min for up to 120 minutes. High dose: 800 mg bolus then 8 mg/min for up to 120 minutes
drugs.notes: Low dose if apixaban 5 mg or less or rivaroxaban 10 mg or less. Withdrawn from US market December 2025 (thrombosis); not available in India.

drugs.name: Protamine sulfate
drugs.dose: UFH: 1 mg per 100 units given in previous 2 to 3 hours (max 50 mg). Enoxaparin: 1 mg per 1 mg if within 8 hours, 0.5 mg per 1 mg if 8 to 12 hours (max 50 mg)

drugs.name: Fresh frozen plasma
drugs.notes: Warfarin reversal only if PCC unavailable.

drugs.name: Activated charcoal
drugs.notes: DOAC ingestion within 2 to 4 hours, airway protected.
